subject: health
unitTitle: Mental Health Maintenance and Sustainable Coping
essentialQuestion: How do I keep myself steady through a transition that removes most of my structure?

prompts.prompt: Explain transition stress and why capable people struggle during it in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies.
Apply sleep, isolation, and workload as leading indicators in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving when to seek professional support and how to start that process as an adult; correct it and explain why.
Connect cost, access, and confidentiality of adult mental-health care with supporting others while protecting your own capacity. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write a transition plan with maintenance strategies, early-warning conditions the learner will watch for, and a concrete first step for getting professional support — including how it would be paid for and accessed.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The plan may be written, spoken, or assembled from supplied strategy cards. General categories may be used throughout instead of specific personal detail.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
